title: H-1B Visa Overhaul Not Targeting India, Says US Ambassador Sergio Gor as Wage-Based Selection Begins

Key Takeaways
  • US Ambassador reassures that H-1B visa changes aren't aimed at India.
  • 70-75% of H-1B visas are issued to Indian nationals annually.
  • New wage-based selection system prioritizes higher-paying job applications.
  • Critics argue changes may harm entry-level Indian tech workers.
  • India-US trade agreement discussions are progressing positively.

US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has sought to reassure Indian professionals that the Trump administration's sweeping changes to the H-1B visa programme are not specifically aimed at India — even as a new wage-based selection system replaces the traditional lottery for fiscal year 2027.

Part of Broader Immigration Reform, Not Country-Specific

Speaking in a recent interview, Gor said the H-1B review is part of the administration's comprehensive immigration overhaul. "The H-1B exercise forms part of the administration's broader immigration reforms. It should not be interpreted as something aimed specifically at Indians," Gor stated. The clarification is particularly significant given that Indian nationals represent approximately 70 to 75 percent of all H-1B visas issued annually. According to recent estimates, around 730,000 Indian H-1B holders currently reside in the United States, supported by approximately 550,000 dependents on H-4 visas.

Key Changes: Wage-Based Over Lottery

The most significant policy shift is the move from a random lottery to a wage-based selection process for cap-subject H-1B visas. Under the new system, applications tied to higher-paying positions receive priority, while lower-paying and entry-level roles face reduced chances of selection. The administration has also introduced a $100,000 filing fee on sponsoring companies. Critics argue that the wage-weighted system disproportionately affects entry-level Indian tech workers and essential sectors like healthcare and research. In response, Congresswoman Bonnie Watson Coleman has introduced the Welcoming International Success Act (WISA), which seeks to cancel the September 2025 immigration proclamation, reduce employer filing fees, and relax wage requirements.

Trade Deal Progress

Impact of Wage-Based Selection
›Shift from lottery to wage-based selection.
›Higher-paying jobs receive selection priority.
›Entry-level roles face reduced chances.
›Critics highlight potential harm to essential sectors.
Gor also signaled that a long-awaited India-US bilateral trade agreement is nearing completion. He noted that recent discussions between US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal had been productive, with only a handful of issues remaining. "A lot of it now is on the language that ultimately both sides will sign," Gor said, expressing optimism that both governments could reach an agreement in the coming weeks or months.

Potential completion of bilateral trade agreement.

What Indian Professionals Should Watch

For the Indian diaspora, the convergence of H-1B reforms and trade negotiations represents a pivotal moment. While the administration maintains that skilled talent remains welcome, the structural changes to the visa system could reshape career planning for thousands of Indian students and professionals considering the US pathway. The WISA bill's progress through Congress will be a key indicator of whether the most restrictive provisions will be softened.
